title: Electricity
seo_title: Electricity Class 10 Science Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 11)
standard_text: Electric current, potential difference and electric current. Ohm's law; resistance, resistivity, factors on which the resistance of a conductor depends. Series combination of resistors, parallel combination of resistors and its applications in daily life. Heating effect of electric current and its applications in daily life. Electric power, interrelation between P, V, I and R.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 10 Science worksheets for NCERT Chapter 11: current and charge, Ohm's law, resistivity, series and parallel resistors, electric power, heating effect and the cost of electricity in kWh. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: V = IR, Q = It, P = VI.
body_html:
How to think about it

Current is the rate of flow of charge (I = Q/t, in amperes). Potential difference is work done per unit charge (V = W/Q, in volts). Ohm's law: V = IR. The resistance of a wire is R = ρL/A, where ρ is the resistivity of the material.

In series, resistances add; in parallel, 1/R = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ + … and the total is less than the smallest. Power P = VI = I²R = V²/R; heat H = I²Rt. Electrical energy is sold in kilowatt hours (units): energy = power (kW) × time (h).

Example

12 V across 4 Ω. Current?

I = V/R

Answer: 3 A

Example

A 1,000 W heater runs 2 h a day for 30 days at ₹6 per unit. Cost?

1 kW × 2 h × 30 = 60 kWh

60 × ₹6

Answer: ₹360

Common mistakes

  • Adding resistances in parallel.
  • Using watts instead of kilowatts for kWh.
  • Connecting an ammeter in parallel.
